name: GdPO4 synthetic monazite
citation: Y. Ni, J. M. Hughes and A. N. Mariano (1995). Crystal chemistry of the monazite and xenotime structures. American Mineralogist 80, 21-26.
conditions_evidence: Numeric measurement temperature/pressure are not given in the inspected CIF or original paper experimental methods; nominal 293/298 K or zero pressure is not inferred.
method: Experimental single-crystal X-ray diffraction, CAD4 diffractometer and graphite-monochromated Mo Kalpha radiation; the original paper independently refines each selected synthetic endmember.
synthesis_conditions_note: The original paper identifies synthetic RE(PO4) crystals supplied by L. Boatner, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, with synthesis methods referenced elsewhere; numeric synthesis conditions not verified.
selection: Selected experimental reference; no FEFF calculation or experimental EXAFS validation performed in source research.
notes: This is the independently measured pure synthetic GdPO4 endmember, not a natural mixed rare-earth specimen and not an element-substituted model.
The entire nine-O coordination polyhedron is retained, including the longest bond near 2.78 A; the next O contact is beyond 3.17 A.
Phosphate first-shell paths describe the selected phosphate environment; they are not validated substitutes for an oxide or fluoride reference.
The source has no atomic occupancy column; full occupancy is the parser/default crystallographic interpretation, not a separately refined occupancy result.

Lanthanide L3 paths are EXAFS candidates, not validated white-line, multiplet, magnetic, or XANES models. FEFF8.2 documents frozen-f density by default and possible f-element SCF convergence difficulties; retain the actual engine recipe and logs.
